findings.evidence: The last changes were not saved and cannot be recovered. Contact support for assistance.
findings.fix: State the cause of the save failure (e.g. a session timeout or a conflicting edit) so the reader can act differently next time.
findings.violation: Reports a loss with no explanation of why it happened or how to avoid it recurring, the account-lockout anchor's shape: a reader who did nothing unusual is left with no way to understand or avoid a repeat.

findings.evidence: This reset link expired an hour after it was sent, so nobody can reuse it from an old message. Request a new link and check the inbox again.
findings.fix: Present this message in a persistent inline note or modal that stays until dismissed, not a self-clearing toast.
findings.violation: The failure fully blocks the reader from continuing (the placement annotation describes a dialog that blocks the new-password field), yet the container is a self-clearing toast, so a reader who looks away misses the one message explaining why they cannot proceed.

findings.evidence: The last changes were not saved and cannot be recovered. Contact support for assistance.
findings.fix: Name the actual cause of the save failure instead of a generic statement that the change was lost.
findings.violation: States that changes were lost with no named cause, the upload-failed anchor's shape: a generic failure statement where a specific, nameable cause was plausibly available.

findings.evidence: This field takes a maximum of 30 characters. Shorten the entry and save again.
findings.fix: Add a brief reason the 30-character limit exists, e.g. what the field feeds into, so the reader understands why it recurs.
findings.violation: States a product-set limit the reader will meet again with no reason attached, the low-stakes shape of the severity-2 anchor (an unexplained password-length minimum).

findings.evidence: The last changes were not saved and cannot be recovered. Contact support for assistance.
findings.fix: Add a brief acknowledgment of the loss (e.g. an apology naming what was lost) alongside the existing contact-support instruction.
findings.violation: The only message block on this screen, with no suggested fix, reports a completed, unrecoverable loss as a bare technical notice with no acknowledgment of what that loss means for the reader, though it does name an avenue (contact support).

findings.evidence: Please correct the highlighted field. Error code: 502.
findings.fix: Replace the code or jargon term with a plain-language sentence a non-technical reader can act on.
findings.violation: The message text carries an internal error code standing in for a plain-language explanation.

findings.evidence: Receipts upload as PDF or PNG only, the two formats the expense system can read. Change this file to one of those formats and upload it again, or select a different receipt.
findings.fix: Validate the file type as soon as it is selected and warn before the reader submits.
findings.violation: The accepted file types are already known to the product and checkable at file-selection time, but this predictable mistake is reported only on-submit with nothing earlier warning the reader.

findings.evidence: Choose a password of at least 8 characters, long enough that a guessing attack cannot work through every combination.
findings.fix: Move the password requirement inline beside or below the password field instead of at the top of the form.
findings.violation: The message sits at the top of a long form, requiring the reader to scroll up to see it, rather than beside the field it concerns, though the field itself stays visible.
